Title: Application database role (readiness 1.1)
Detail: Migration creates `srs_app` (NOSUPERUSER, NOBYPASSRLS) with DML grants on all tables and default privileges for future ones; migrations keep running as the owner. The compose stack and test helper connect the API as a login role that inherits `srs_app`. Done when: `\du` shows `srs_app` without bypass; the API in compose runs as it. Fixes SEC-1. Delivered 2026-11-19 on branch phase-1-security-isolation (PR #51).

Title: Run the API suite under RLS (readiness 1.2)
Detail: `startTestApp` migrates as superuser and builds the app with a second connection as `srs_app`. Fix every query that fails: move it into `withTenantContext`, or a named, audited system context for genuine cross-tenant jobs (retention, tenant listing). Done when: The full API suite passes connected as `srs_app`. Fixes SEC-1. Delivered 2026-11-19 on branch phase-1-security-isolation (PR #51).

Title: RLS on the remaining tenant tables (readiness 1.3)
Detail: Enable and force RLS on `notification`, `communication_dispatch_log`, `audit_record` (tenant rows, plus a policy for platform rows), `communication_template` (null-tenant read) and the demo tables. Add a CI check that fails on any table with `tenant_id` but no RLS. Done when: Catalogue check in CI; isolation tests per table. Fixes SEC-1. Delivered 2026-11-19 on branch phase-1-security-isolation (PR #51).

Title: Cross-tenant isolation test (readiness 1.4)
Detail: A generated test signs in as tenant B and calls every GET route with tenant A's IDs (from the OpenAPI spec and fixtures); none may return A's data. Done when: Runs in CI and covers every route. Fixes SEC-1. Delivered 2026-11-19 on branch phase-1-security-isolation (PR #51).

Title: Strict token validation (readiness 1.5)
Detail: Pin `issuer`, `audience` and `algorithms: ['RS256']` (configurable per service), and add a clock tolerance. Apply to all services through `@revelation-srs/auth`. Done when: Tests: wrong issuer, audience or algorithm gets 401. Fixes SEC-2. Delivered 2026-11-19 on branch phase-1-security-isolation (PR #51).

Title: Refuse insecure configuration (readiness 1.6)
Detail: Outside `development` and `test`, refuse to start without a JWKS URL, or with the default or a short HS256 secret. Same in the modules. Done when: Start-up test per service. Fixes SEC-3. Delivered 2026-11-19 on branch phase-1-security-isolation (PR #51).

Title: Validate wellbeing input (readiness 1.7)
Detail: TypeBox schemas for all 53 wellbeing routes (UUIDs, enums from the state machines, lengths); problem+json errors; generate its OpenAPI. Done when: 0 routes without a schema (a CI check like `check:coded-values`); a bad UUID returns 400, not 500. Fixes SEC-4. Delivered 2026-11-19 on branch phase-1-security-isolation (PR #51).

Title: Fix the engagement proxy (readiness 1.8)
Detail: Authenticate in core before forwarding; forward an allow-list of headers only; stream the body unchanged; 15 s timeout; body limit. Done when: Proxy tests: unauthenticated gets 401; multipart passes through; timeout gets 504. Fixes SEC-5. Delivered 2026-11-19 on branch phase-1-security-isolation (PR #51).

Title: Transactional outbox for domain events (readiness 2.1)
Detail: Each publish site writes an `event_outbox` row in the same transaction as the change (generalising the existing workflow outbox); a relay in the worker publishes and marks rows, with retries and an event ID for de-duplication; consumers de-duplicate on that ID. Done when: Test: NATS down during a change, NATS back, event delivered exactly once to a consumer. Fixes AVL-2.

Title: Readiness without NATS (readiness 2.2)
Detail: `/ready` checks only the database (and Keycloak JWKS reachability, cached). NATS, the outbox lag and Temporal are reported on `/health/details` and in metrics with alerts. Done when: Pods stay ready with NATS stopped (compose test). Fixes AVL-1. Done 2026-11-21: /ready gates on the database only; NATS and Keycloak JWKS are reported with required: false, as Temporal already was (ADR-027). readiness.int.test.ts: ready with NATS down; it fails on the old route. Outbox lag and alerting are part of BL-009 and BL-087.

Title: Timeouts everywhere (readiness 2.3)
Detail: A shared `fetchWithTimeout` (default 10 s), used for every outbound call; a database connect timeout, a `statement_timeout` per pool (for example 30 s API, 5 min worker) and `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout`. Done when: A lint rule bans bare `fetch` in services; pool settings are tested. Fixes AVL-3. Done 2026-11-21: fetchWithTimeout (10 s default) in @revelation-srs/auth, with a copy in the dependency-free VLE adapter; every service call uses it, including the adapter's VLE drivers' default; ESLint no-restricted-globals bans bare fetch in service code. Pools: 10 s connect timeout always; statement 30 s and idle-in-transaction 60 s for the API and modules (DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS, 5 minutes for the worker); migrations and bulk loads leave them off. timeouts.int.test.ts covers both.

Title: Spread and replicate (readiness 2.4)
Detail: Topology spread constraints for the API, admin, portal, worker and modules; NATS at 3 replicas with the JetStream stream declared as infrastructure (replicas 3, retention and limits) rather than created by the app. Done when: Manifest review; kubeval and Kustomize build in CI. Fixes AVL-4, AVL-5. Done 2026-11-21: topology spread (nodes and zones, ScheduleAnyway) on all seven service Deployments; SRS_EVENTS declared by an idempotent srs-nats-streams Job (file storage, 30-day and 8 GB limits, 2-minute duplicate window), 3 replicas on the production 3-node NATS cluster; the network policy admits the Job to NATS. check:k8s builds every overlay and checks spread and stream replicas. While doing it, found the manifests could not be deployed at all (BL-334, also fixed).

Title: Idempotent, leader-elected jobs (readiness 2.5)
Detail: The reconciler takes a Postgres advisory lock per run, or uses `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` on its work rows; overdue notices become a Kubernetes CronJob. Done when: Test: two reconcilers in parallel do the work once. Fixes SCL-3, SCL-4. Design settled by ADR-027: per-job pg_try_advisory_lock on a reserved connection in the worker's scheduler (not a Kubernetes CronJob), correctness from claiming rows first; the overdue digest becomes claim-then-send and the escalation sweep is scheduled.

Title: Pagination contract (readiness 3.1)
Detail: One cursor-pagination convention (`limit`, default 50, maximum 200, with `cursor`) for every tenant-wide list; responses carry `nextCursor`; admin tables page or load more; a CI check fails on new unbounded list routes. Done when: All 70 routes paged; the check is in CI. Fixes PERF-1.

Title: Index review (readiness 3.2)
Detail: Add indexes for the 135 unindexed foreign keys where the child table can grow, and `(tenant_id, …)` leading indexes on the 28 tables; a CI check reports unindexed foreign keys on growing tables. Done when: Catalogue check in CI; `EXPLAIN` on the top 20 queries uses indexes. Fixes PERF-2.

Title: Load test baseline (readiness 3.3)
Detail: Extend the k6 suites (`infra/k6`) to the `institution-year` scenario: p95 targets per route class (reads < 300 ms, writes < 800 ms), run nightly. Done when: A nightly report, with regressions flagged. Fixes PERF-1 to PERF-3.

Title: Remove N+1 loops (readiness 3.4)
Detail: Batch the 64 loops where they run per request (set-based queries, `inArray`); add a batch student-summary endpoint and use it in `usePersonNames`. Done when: Query counts asserted in tests for the main hot paths. Fixes PERF-3, PERF-4.

Title: Shared cache invalidation (readiness 3.5)
Detail: Publish an invalidation message on change (NATS core subject, or Postgres `LISTEN/NOTIFY`) to which every pod listens; academic-rule lookups go uncached, or cached with immediate invalidation. Done when: Test: a change on pod A is visible on pod B at once. Fixes SCL-2. Design settled by ADR-027: pg_notify in the writing transaction, a direct listener connection, cache cleared on every reconnect and bypassed while disconnected, TTLs kept as a backstop.

Title: Cross-pod notifications (readiness 3.6)
Detail: Deliver notification events to all pods (NATS subject, or `LISTEN/NOTIFY`); each pod pushes to its own connections. Done when: Test with two API instances. Fixes SCL-1. Design settled by ADR-027: pg_notify carrying identifiers only; a pod reads the row under tenant context only for people it holds connections for; clients resync on reconnect.

Title: Distributed rate limiting (readiness 3.7)
Detail: Rate-limit store in Redis or Valkey (or Postgres); key by user after authentication and by IP before it; separate budgets for writes and the public verification routes. Done when: Limits hold across pods. Fixes SEC-6. Found in phase 1: the limiter runs before authentication, so every caller is counted by IP address, never by user or tenant. Design settled by ADR-027: an unlogged Postgres counter table behind a custom @fastify/rate-limit store; limiter moves to preHandler keyed by user; budgets 1,200 a minute per user, 300 writes a minute, 30 a minute per IP on /public/v1; per-IP limits before authentication at the ingress; fail open with a metric and alert. Needs BL-168 (trustProxy) first.

Title: Squash and split migrations (readiness 4.1)
Detail: Before the next schema change, squash 0000–0009 into a new baseline (the procedure is in the data migration plan) and set a rule: one migration per feature, never edit an applied one. Fixes MNT-2. Delivered 2026-11-19 on branch phase-1-security-isolation (PR #51), before phase 1: migrations 0000–0009 squashed into 0000_baseline.

Title: Break up the largest files (readiness 4.2)
Detail: Split `StudentDetailPage` into a file per tab, `module-selection/service.ts` by concern (diets, windows, allocation), and the route files by resource; `app.ts` registers domain plugins (see 4.4). Fixes MNT-1.

Title: One error shape (readiness 4.3)
Detail: A shared problem+json error handler in `@revelation-srs/auth` (or a new `@revelation-srs/http` package), used by all services. Fixes MNT-3.

Title: Domain plugins (readiness 4.4)
Detail: Each domain exports a Fastify plugin that constructs its services and registers its routes from declared dependencies; `buildApp` composes plugins. This makes adding or removing a capability a one-line change. Fixes EXT-2.

Title: Remove two-way dependencies (readiness 4.5)
Detail: Break the four cycles with events or a small shared interface; add an import-boundary lint rule (`eslint-plugin-boundaries`, or depcruise) so new cycles fail CI. Fixes EXT-1.

Title: Encrypt special-category content (readiness 4.6)
Detail: Envelope encryption (OpenBao Transit) for session notes and disability notes in the wellbeing service; keys rotated; reads are already audited. Fixes SEC-8.

Title: Clear the lint warnings (readiness 4.7)
Detail: Fix or explicitly allow the 87 warnings, then make `--max-warnings 0` the CI rule. Fixes MNT-4.

Title: Hide internal endpoints in production (readiness 4.8)
Detail: Serve the OpenAPI document and demo status only when docs or demo are enabled. Fixes SEC-9.

Title: Content-Security-Policy, HSTS and security headers on the SPAs (readiness 1.9, part)
Detail: CSP, HSTS, frame and related headers set in infra/docker/{admin,portal}/nginx.conf, not only at the ingress. Delivered 2026-11-19 (PR #51). The CSP allows inline styles (a dialog component injects a style tag) and any HTTPS host for API calls; narrow connect-src once deployment hosts are known.

Title: Backend-for-frontend for the admin app and portal; no tokens in the browser (readiness 1.9, remainder)
Detail: Implement ADR-026: apps/bff deployed per app as a confidential client, nginx proxying /bff/, Postgres session store with encrypted tokens and locked refresh, CSRF by Origin plus a custom header, BroadcastChannel multi-tab logout, back-channel logout, CSP connect-src narrowed to self. Done when: no token in browser storage or JavaScript; cookie, CSRF and refresh tests pass; header checks in CI.

Title: Decide token storage for the admin app and portal (readiness decision 1)
Detail: In memory with silent refresh, or a backend-for-frontend with HTTP-only cookies. The audit recommends in memory now, and a backend-for-frontend if a penetration test asks for it. Decided 2026-11-20 in ADR-026: a same-origin backend-for-frontend per app (confidential Keycloak client, HTTP-only __Host- session cookie, tokens held server-side), departing from the audit's in-memory recommendation because RFC 10017 (BCP 212) strongly recommends a BFF for apps handling personal data.

Title: Decide the shared cache and rate-limit store (readiness decision 2)
Detail: Redis or Valkey, or Postgres (LISTEN/NOTIFY and a counter table). The audit recommends Postgres first. Blocks readiness 3.5 and 3.7. Decided 2026-11-20 in ADR-027: PostgreSQL for all four functions (pg_notify for invalidation and fan-out, an unlogged counter table for rate limits, advisory locks plus row claiming for jobs); no Redis or Valkey unless the readiness 3.3 load test shows the counter table costs more than 15% of database writes or 2 ms at p95.

Title: Kubernetes sets ALLOWED_ORIGINS but the API reads CORS_ORIGINS
Detail: apps/api/src/config.ts reads CORS_ORIGINS (default http://localhost:5173); infra/k8s/base/api.yaml and the staging and production overlays set ALLOWED_ORIGINS. In Kubernetes the API would refuse browser calls from the real admin and portal origins. Fix the name, and add a check that every variable the manifests set is one the config reads. Done 2026-11-21: manifests use CORS_ORIGINS. New pnpm check:deployment-env (CI) fails on any variable a service Deployment sets that its source never reads; putting ALLOWED_ORIGINS back makes it fail. It also found and fixed: wellbeing set PORT but reads WELLBEING_PORT, and the API set HOST, KEYCLOAK_URL, KEYCLOAK_REALM, KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID and WELLBEING_URL, which nothing reads.

Title: Run the wellbeing and attendance test suites under RLS
Detail: Both module suites still connect as the database superuser, so their row-level security is not proven the way readiness 1.2 proves it for the API. Connect them as a login role inheriting the module app role and fix what fails. Done 2026-11-20: both module suites connect as a login role inheriting srs_app. Running under RLS found that every module policy failed outside a tenant context (now NULLIF, migration 0002 in each module) and that the wellbeing adjustment and EC hand-offs read and marked their outbox rows outside a tenant context, so a delivered hand-off was never marked sent (a retry would send it again). The outbox repository functions now accept only a tenant transaction. Wellbeing 271 and attendance 27 tests pass.

Title: RLS on the two wellbeing outbox tables, and extend the coverage check to module schemas
Detail: wellbeing.srs_handoff_outbox and wellbeing.srs_ec_handoff_outbox have a tenant_id but no RLS. rls-coverage.int.test.ts covers the core schemas only; make it (or a module equivalent) cover every schema with a tenant_id. Done 2026-11-20: wellbeing migration 0002 enables and forces RLS on both outboxes (and forces it on sar_export_log, found unforced by the new coverage test); modules/wellbeing/test/rls-coverage.int.test.ts and modules/attendance/test/rls-coverage.int.test.ts check every module table with a tenant_id.

Title: Sign off the EC claim permission role mapping
Detail: Phase 1 added ec-claim:read and ec-claim:manage (wellbeing-advisor, registry-administrator) after finding the seven EC claim routes checked no permission. Confirm the roles, and whether deciding a claim needs its own permission separate from managing it. Decided 2026-11-20 in ADR-028: new roles ec-case-officer and ec-decision-maker; new permission ec-claim:determine (decision maker only) with separation of duties from everyone who recorded, changed or assessed the claim; registry-administrator loses the wellbeing EC permissions; panel or delegated officer becomes the tenant setting ec.decisionAuthority. Implementation is BL-169 and BL-170; the institution confirmation is BL-174.

Title: Language choice in the admin app and portal
Detail: Screens follow the app language, but neither app offers a language choice, so translated wording shows only once one does.

Title: Move portal outcome sentences into the wording table
Detail: Outcome sentences the portal shows students ("You accepted this offer") are still in its translation files, not the merged wording table.

Detail: ADR-016 (authoritative business state separate from workflow) is accepted but not applied in every domain.

Title: Propagate identity merge decisions to dependent records
Detail: A merge creates an identity_redirect row, but nothing consumes it, so dependent records are not updated. See also the governed identity merge row added from the 2026-11-21 BP-08 pre-review. Decided 2026-11-22 by ADR-031 (Proposed: decision authority and unmerge policy await the registry process owner and DPO). Work is BL-353 to BL-363; BL-355 is the propagation itself.

Title: Year-level credit and joint-honours checks with unregistered periods
Detail: Year-level credit and joint-honours checks assume the year's other periods are registered.

Title: Allocation precedence for students whose diet includes the module
Detail: Allocation gives no precedence to students whose diet includes the module.

Title: Refresh exam entries when an adjustment is approved
Detail: Exam entries are generated per exam board from its data pack; entries generated before an adjustment was approved are not refreshed, so its exams distribution stays pending (visibly). Done 2026-11-21: ExamEntryService.applyExamAdditions adds a newly approved adjustment to the enrolment's current entries for exams not yet sat (in force on the exam date; unscheduled: not yet ended), called after recording and by the worker's reconcile loop; never rewrites an exam already sat; idempotent; a late time adjustment with no amount reports the exams distribution failed. Also fixed a latent clock bug: closing an entry version recorded by the database clock could violate the temporal check. Not covered: an amendment to an adjustment's amount (a new adjustment is the path); telling the timetabling system about a changed entry it already scheduled is BL-336.

Title: Test the Canvas driver against a real instance
Detail: The Canvas driver is tested against fakes only; clearing via extra_time: 0 is undocumented. Moodle is the only VLE in scope.

Title: Employed students: hours from other employers and holiday-period visa rules

Title: Real virus scanning of uploaded evidence
Detail: packages/documents uses a NoopScanner placeholder; a ClamAV-style scanner is a deployment seam not yet wired in. Evidence uploads (adjustments, wellbeing) are not scanned. Decided 2026-11-22 by ADR-030 (Proposed: two ClamAV policy defaults and the alert receiver await the information security lead): synchronous clamd scan before the write transaction, fail closed, retrieve() serves only clean or system-generated. Work is BL-338 to BL-352. 2026-11-22: the P0 work is done (BL-338 to BL-343): every upload is scanned before it is stored and nothing unscanned is served. Open until the alerts (BL-344), UI messages and value set (BL-346) and real-node latency (BL-345) are done, per ADR-030 stage 5.

Title: Tighten the Keycloak realm: 5-minute access tokens, refresh-token rotation, no offline_access, exact redirect URIs
Detail: Today the realm issues 8-hour access tokens (accessTokenLifespan 28800) without refresh-token rotation, and packages/ui/src/auth/oidc.ts requests offline_access, so a stolen token lasts a working day. Independent of the BFF and worth doing first. Done 2026-11-20: access tokens 300 s, refresh-token rotation with no reuse, offline_access no longer requested, redirect URIs exact (/callback) with an explicit logout redirect. Verified against Keycloak 26.0.7 with the changed realm. Keycloak treats a reused refresh token as theft and also revokes its replacement, so tabs must never refresh concurrently: refreshFromStorage (packages/ui) serialises refreshes across tabs with a Web Lock. Two real browser tabs on one session made one refresh and both stayed signed in. Before a deployment adopts this realm, its own Keycloak needs the same settings; the existing local Keycloak volume keeps the old realm until it is re-imported.

Title: Realm configuration test
Detail: A test over infra/compose/keycloak/srs-realm.json: confidential clients only, no wildcard redirect URIs, access tokens of at most 300 seconds, refresh-token rotation on, no offline_access. Done 2026-11-22: scripts/check-realm.mjs (pnpm check:realm, in CI): browser clients confidential, redirect only to /bff/auth/callback with no wildcards, back-channel logout with the session required, access tokens at most 300 s, rotation with no reuse, SSO limits 1800/36000 s, no offline_access offered or requested by the BFF. It reports six problems on the realm as it was before.

Title: Retention disposal: two-person approval of a sweep plan, and a disposal certificate per person
Detail: The rest of BL-284. A dry run should produce a stored plan; a different person holding a new approval permission approves it; execution applies only that plan, writes record_disposition (anonymised) with a certificate reference per person, and refuses if eligibility changed. Needs a migration for the plan and approval. Done 2026-11-22: core migration 0004 (retention_disposal_plan and items, RLS, status value set; record_disposition gains person_id, disposal_plan_id, certificate_ref). POST /admin/retention/plans prepares from the dry run (retention:enforce); approve or reject by someone else holding the new retention:approve (403 separation-of-duties for the preparer, also a CHECK constraint); execute applies only the approved plan (hash-checked), once, all or nothing, refused with 409 if anyone's eligibility changed, and writes a record_disposition with certificate RDC-<plan>-<n> per person. /enforce?dryRun=false is refused (409). retention:approve is DPO for now; whether a records manager should hold it is for the DPO to confirm.

Title: VLE adapter deployment lacks its required settings and uses a static service token
Detail: Found verifying BL-176. adapters/vle requires TENANT_ID, INTEGRATION_REGISTRATION_ID and SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN, but the srs-vle-adapter Deployment sets none of them, so it would fail at start. SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN is a static bearer token, which cannot work with 5-minute access tokens (BL-159); apply the ADR-029 approach (client credentials bound to the tenant). Extend check:deployment-env to fail on required variables a Deployment does not set, allowing for secrets injected from files. Partly done 2026-11-21: the Deployment sets TENANT_ID and INTEGRATION_REGISTRATION_ID from srs-vle-adapter-config (placeholders refused at start: both must be UUIDs); VLE_API_KEY renamed to VLE_API_TOKEN, which the connector reads; check:deployment-env now counts exported secrets and fails on any required variable a Deployment does not set, with SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN listed as the one known gap. Still open: the service identity for the connector (a vle-service role and narrow reply permission instead of integration:manage and mark:write), which needs an architect decision extending ADR-029. The service identity is decided by ADR-032 (Accepted 2026-11-22). Work is BL-364 to BL-369. Done 2026-11-22 with BL-364 to BL-368 (ADR-032).
